# Git for things you cannot put on GitHub: what changed in v1.4.0

1 unchanged paragraph

Summary: An introduction to sgit and sgit.ai —sgit.ai, what an encrypted vault is, why version control had to be rebuilt to get one, and what nineteen published vaults look like when the server storing them cannot read a byte.

2 unchanged paragraphs

All of it wants exactly what git gives you —you, history, branches, diffs, the ability to hand somebody a link and know what they will see. And all of it is the reason people say *"we can't put that in GitHub."* So it ends up in a shared drive, an email thread, or a Notion page nobody can diff, and the version history that mattered is gone.

1 unchanged paragraph

!shot site-home.webp | images/ | sgit.ai —sgit.ai,`pip install sgit-ai`. Pure Python, two runtime dependencies, Apache-2.0.

1 unchanged paragraph, under The part that is easy to say and hard to build

Zero knowledge is a claim people make loosely, so here is the precise version: **the server holds ciphertext and nothing else.** Not your filenames, not your directory structure, not your commit messages. Encryption and decryption happen on your machine. There is no key escrow, no admin override, no support engineer who can recover it for you —you, and that last part is a feature with a real cost, which is worth being honest about up front.

2 unchanged paragraphs

That is the **vault key**, and it is three things at once —once, the address of the vault, the authorisation to write to it, and the key that decrypts it. Lose it and the data is gone. Leak it and someone can rewrite your history.

From it you can derive, one way, a **read key**: same vault, read-only, safe to publish. That asymmetry is the whole sharing model. Every vault linked from sgit.ai is published as a read key, and no vault key has ever been published —published, a rule enforced by a tripwire in the release pipeline that scans every file before either remote is touched.

5 unchanged paragraphs, under Ten seconds of proof

That second screenshot is the argument. The object is **content-addressed over its ciphertext**, which means the host can deduplicate it, cache it for a year, and serve it from a CDN —CDN, while remaining unable to tell you what it is. You get the operational benefits of a normal object store without granting it the usual price of admission.

2 unchanged paragraphs, under Nineteen vaults you can open right now

The best way to understand a vault is to open one. **Every vault on sgit.ai is live** —live**: the screenshots are of real vaults, opened with the read keys published beside them.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under The part that surprises people

A vault can contain an *application*, not just documents —documents, and that application runs against the vault without ever being handed a credential.

!shot permissions.webp | ../demos/vaults/risk-graph-explorer/images/ | `"permissions": {}` —{}`, the app requests nothing, and is granted nothing.

Look at `"permissions": {}` in that file. The app asks for no filesystem access at all. It still renders the whole risk graph, because the host reads the vault and passes results in. The app never sees a key. **Capability without credential** —credential**, and it means you can run code you did not write against data you care about, with the blast radius set by a config file you can read in one screen.

• [**risks.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#risk-governance) —[**risks.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#risk-governance), *"You cannot deny a risk. You can only say how long you accept it."*

• [**llms.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#agents-ai) —[**llms.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#agents-ai), your app calls a language model without ever holding an API key.

• [**issues-fs.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#graphs-method)[**issues-fs.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#graphs-method).— theThe issues are files, and the files are a graph.

• [**open-source.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#business-publishing) —[**open-source.sgit.ai**](../../../network/index.md#business-publishing), *"Open source is a strategy. It is not a charity."*

• [**sg-sentinel.sgit.ai**](../../../network/sg-sentinel.md) —[**sg-sentinel.sgit.ai**](../../../network/sg-sentinel.md), an edge guard design that says `NOT BUILT` at the top of every page.

3 unchanged paragraphs, under Try it

``` pip install sgit-ai sgit clone sgit_rk1_c004daae386e8d17fa648884acc527018bd4ea1116ad673fb2f1b068011695c9:73heuprzsgit_public_read_c004daae386e8d17fa648884acc527018bd4ea1116ad673fb2f1b068011695c9:73heuprz```

That is the EU AI Act vault —vault, 207 files on your disk in under a minute, from a key printed on a public web page, with no account anywhere.

1 unchanged paragraph

> **Status, plainly.** sgit is beta and says so on every page. The CLI is `pip install sgit-ai`, Apache-2.0, pure Python. The site you are reading is itself served from a vault, released 59 times, and each release is [logged in full](../../../admin/versions.md) —full](/admin/versions.html), including the ones that broke something.
